title: Internal Audit -  Manager
description: At Ripple, we’re building a world where value moves like information does today. It’s big, it’s bold, and we’re already doing it. Through our crypto solutions for financial institutions, businesses, governments and developers, we are improving the global financial system and creating greater economic fairness and opportunity for more people, in more places around the world. And we get to do the best work of our career and grow our skills surrounded by colleagues who have our backs.  If you’re ready to see your impact and unlock incredible career growth opportunities, join us, and build real world value. THE WORK: Ripple’s Internal Audit Team within the Legal and Compliance organization is searching for an Internal Audit Information Technology (IT) Manager to implement the risk-based audit plan as the 3rd line of defense for the company! The IT Internal Auditor will work under the supervision of the Internal Audit leadership to complete technical audits and build relationships with leaders across the organization. To succeed, qualified candidates may exhibit the ability to problem-solve as part of a team, demonstrate the capability to actively pursue their career development, exhibit technical proficiency in audit procedures, and interact with client personnel in a professional manner. WHAT YOU'LL DO: Manage IT audits successfully through conducting interviews, identifying key risks and controls, drafting work papers, gathering evidence, performing testing and reviewing workpapers. Prepare audit work papers adhering to international auditing standards for quality and content, ensuring accuracy and completeness. Evaluate and detail the design and efficiency of internal controls, identifying control gaps and opportunities for process improvement. Collaborate with Information Security & GRC partners to assess audit findings, communicate control weaknesses, and assist in developing management action plans for mitigation while evaluating the adequacy of responses. Prepare comprehensive audit reports outlining findings and recommendations, presenting results to senior management for review and action. Coordinate with external auditors and regulatory bodies to support examination efforts, ensuring compliance and transparency in audit processes. Manage and mentor junior staff, providing guidance and professional development. WHAT YOU'LL BRING: Bachelor's Degree in Management Information Systems, Computer Science, Accounting, Finance, or equivalent business field. Minimum 5 years experience conducting internal or external risk-based IT audits. Experience performing audits across Financial Services, Banking & Capital Markets industry is preferred. Proven knowledge of accounting principles and Generally Accepted Auditing Standards. Solid understanding of Sarbanes-Oxley and/or COSO/COBIT internal control framework is a plus. Certifications such as Certified Internal Auditor (CIA), Certified Public Accountant (CPA), Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA), Certified Information Security Manager (CISM), and/or Certified Information Security Professional (CISSP) are a plus. Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills. Exceptional leadership and team management abilities. Strong communication and interpersonal skills. For positions that will be based in CA, the annual salary range for this position is below. Actual salaries may vary based on numerous factors including, among other things, an individual applicant’s experience and qualifications for the position. This range does not include equity or additional compensation, such as bonuses or commissions.  CA Annual Base Salary Range $140,000 — $175,000 USD WHO WE ARE: Do Your Best Work The opportunity to build in a fast-paced start-up environment with experienced industry leaders A learning environment where you can dive deep into the latest technologies and make an impact.  A professional development budget to support other modes of learning. Thrive in an environment where no matter what race, ethnicity, gender, origin, or culture they identify with, every employee is a respected, valued, and empowered part of the team. In-office collaboration for moments that matter is important to our culture, and we give managers and teams the flexibility to decide which 10+ days a month they come in.  Bi-weekly all-company meeting - business updates and ask me anything style discussion with our Leadership Team We come together for moments that matter which include team offsites, team bonding activities, happy hours and more! title: Business Risk and Controls Manager- Commercial Payments and Deposits
description: Position Summary The Business Risk and Controls Manager is responsible for developing and maintaining treasury management, payments, and deposits business risk processes to minimize the organization's exposure to regulatory criticism, reputational harm and financial risk of loss. This position serves as the business line’s risk management subject matter expert for a variety of payment products and processes, industry rules, standards, and best practices. The Business Risk and Controls Manager also provides end-to-end consultative advice across treasury management and payments processes to manage a variety of risk and compliance topics. Duties & Responsibilities Assess controls frameworks throughout both the commercial payments business line as well as FirsTech/Busey Payments; coordinate improvement plans to address gaps or weaknesses identified Provide guidance on control improvements to ensure control design objectives adequately mitigate risks identified in an operationally efficient manner Provide recommended solutions to resolve findings or deficiencies; implement monitoring to prevent reoccurrence after findings are remediated Collaborate with business line staff to develop risk-based control testing standards to evaluate the design and operating effectiveness of controls; includes sample testing, end-to-end process reviews, and establishing key metrics and indicators Develop end-to-end risk management reporting to inform management and oversight bodies of the direction of risk as identified through client composition, transaction types/volumes, and monitoring of third-party originators, ACH/RDC returns, credit reviews, fraud events/losses, etc Provide direct assistance to business lines in support of fulfilling enterprise-wide efforts to identify, assess, measure, monitor, and report risk; when levels of risk are outside of appetite, assist in implementing mitigating controls to reduce risk levels; includes annual risk assessments Serve as a liaison between the business line and second line of defense to ensure appropriate coordination on changes in law, rules, and regulation by translating the regulatory impact into the business lines’ operations. Ensure the business line operates in compliance with regulatory agencies and bodies that oversee payments as well as internal policies and standards Support change management processes necessitated by the impact of new products and services, new standards or technologies, new or changing rules or regulations Assist in establishing and maintaining process documentation that supports both consistency and continuity of operations, identifies interdependencies, and serves as evidential documentation for internal and external assessors and auditors Create and maintain reporting that captures the status of a variety of risk and compliance projects and initiatives to keep business line staff and management, credit partners and second line partners informed about first line priorities and progress Assist and support Treasury Management, Deposits, and FirsTech/Busey Payments projects as needed Education & Experience Knowledge of: Strong oral and written communication skills; can adapt communication and presentation style to fit various audiences In-depth and up-to-date knowledge of treasury management industry rules and standards, as well as banking laws and regulations specific to payment and deposit activities Design and documentation of procedures and controls that promote consistent, repeatable, and auditable processes Ability to: Develop new procedures and approaches to remediate a variety of issues and findingsDevelop testing and quality review programs and related metrics to measure effectiveness of business processes Problem-solve by making sound and timely recommendations or decisions to keep forward progress; is discerning and applies situational knowledge to determine appropriate action or escalation Identify process efficiency and automation opportunities to strengthen control effectiveness Establish routine, relevant and actionable risk reporting suitable for a variety of audiences Establish and maintain collaborative partnerships at all levels throughout the organization; facilitate cooperation between process leaders when conflicting views and priorities arise Work with a high degree of independence Education and Training: Bachelor’s degree or the equivalent combination of education and experience; Business or Finance degree preferred 8-10 years’ experience in financial services with experience with commercial payments and/or deposit products and services, payment collection and aggregation products and service knowledge a plus Large-bank experience (> $10B) and current AAP (Accredited ACH Professional) certification preferred Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite required, Smartsheet, PowerBi and other project and reporting tool experience preferred Every day, our associates live Busey’s core values, doing better business, building stronger relations

title: Senior Manager, Regulatory Compliance and Licensing
description: Who We Are At Justworks, you’ll enjoy a welcoming and casual environment, great benefits, wellness program offerings, company retreats, and the ability to interact with and learn from leaders in the startup community. We work hard and care about our most prized asset - our people. We’re helping businesses get off the ground by enabling them to focus on running their business. We solve HR issues. We’re data-driven and never stop iterating. If you’d like to work in a supportive, entrepreneurial environment, are interested in building something meaningful and having fun while doing it, we’d love to hear from you. We're united by shared goals and shared motivations at Justworks. These are best summed up in our company values, which are reflected in our product and in our team. Our Values If this sounds like you, you’ll fit right in. Who You Are You’re a seasoned compliance leader who knows that strong regulatory functions depend on clear ownership, capable teams, disciplined execution, and sound judgment. You bring meaningful experience leading regulatory compliance operations in a highly regulated environment. You can translate complex requirements into practical processes, challenge and support subject matter experts, and build the management systems needed to execute regulatory obligations consistently. You are equally comfortable developing teams, engaging with regulators and external partners, partnering with Legal and business leaders, and communicating risks and priorities to senior leadership. You enjoy strengthening functions that are evolving, creating clarity where processes or ownership are fragmented, and building a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. Your Success Profile What You Will Work On Lead Regulatory Compliance and Licensing  Provide people and operational leadership across Regulatory Compliance and Licensing Operations within Product Compliance. Set clear priorities, ownership, operating rhythms, and performance expectations across the functions. Develop team members and build the capabilities, judgment, and accountability needed for consistent regulatory execution. Partner with Product Compliance leadership on organizational design, resourcing, and the continued evolution of these functions. Strengthen the Operating Foundation Establish clear ownership, documented processes, effective controls, escalation paths, and backup coverage for critical regulatory obligations. Reduce single points of failure through cross-training, business continuity planning, and sustainable knowledge management. Improve visibility into upcoming obligations, execution status, risks, and issues requiring leadership attention. Standardize and simplify workflows where doing so improves reliability, efficiency, and compliance outcomes. Develop meaningful operational measures that help assess execution, capacity, quality, and risk. Drive Regulatory Execution and Readiness Ensure timely, accurate, and compliant execution of key obligations, including PEO and other applicable licensing, CPEO certification, ESAC accreditation, regulatory reporting, government filings, business registrations, regulatory examinations, and agency correspondence. Ensure regulatory obligations are appropriately documented, calendared, assigned, reviewed, and escalated. Oversee interactions with regulators, government agencies, auditors, and external partners as appropriate, and ensure follow-up actions are completed. Identify emerging regulatory and operational risks early and ensure appropriate mitigation and escalation. Lead Regulatory Change Lead the function in monitoring and interpreting relevant regulatory developments and assessing their impact on Justworks’ products and operations. Ensure changes are communicated to the appropriate stakeholders and translated into clear operational, product, or control requirements. Partner with Payroll Compliance, Legal, Product, Engineering, Operations, and other stakeholders to support implementation of new or changing requirements. Establish clear processes for tracking regulatory change from identification through assessment, ownership, implementation, and closure. Strengthen Controls and Remediation Partner with Product Compliance leadership, Internal Audit, Legal, Finance, Product, Security, and other stakeholders to strengthen controls and address identified risks within the functions. Support audit and examination readiness through clear documentation, evidence, ownership, and timely follow-up. Ensure remediation actions owned by the functions are appropriately prioritized, assigned, tracked, and sustained. Promote proactive risk identification and escalation rather than reliance on reactive issue management. Partner Across the Business Build trusted partnerships across Legal, Product, Engineering, Payroll Compliance, Finance, Security, Internal Audit, Customer Success, Government Affairs, and Operations. title: Vice President, Technology Risk Managment
description: Our Purpose Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential. Title and Summary Vice President, Technology Risk Managment Overview The Vice President, Technology Risk Management leads the Program Controls, Operations & Modernization (ProCOM) Technology Risk Management function and is responsible for establishing, governing, and continuously enhancing the risk, controls, resilience, and operational governance capabilities that support Mastercard's technology organization. This role provides strategic leadership for enterprise technology risk management, ensuring risks are proactively identified, assessed, managed, and reported while maintaining alignment with regulatory expectations, enterprise risk frameworks, and Mastercard's commitment to operational excellence. The position serves as a key partner to technology, product, engineering, security, and business leaders to drive a strong culture of risk ownership, control effectiveness, production readiness, resilience, and continuous improvement. Through standardized governance practices, risk intelligence, operational insights, and control frameworks, this role enables informed decision-making, strengthens organizational accountability, and supports the scalable growth of Mastercard's products, platforms, and technology services. The Vice President is accountable for advancing ProCOM's vision of delivering integrated risk management, governance, operational readiness, and modernization capabilities that improve technology outcomes and enhance customer trust. Role - Define and execute the strategic vision, operating model, and roadmap for Technology Risk Management within ProCOM. - Lead the development, implementation, and governance of technology risk frameworks, methodologies, standards, procedures, and controls across the technology organization. - Establish and oversee enterprise-wide processes for technology risk identification, assessment, treatment, monitoring, escalation, and reporting. - Drive consistent adoption of risk management, operational resilience, production readiness, and control practices across products, platforms, and engineering organizations. - Provide executive oversight of technology risk portfolios, key risk indicators, control effectiveness measures, issue remediation activities, and emerging risk trends. - Lead governance forums and executive reporting processes that communicate technology risk posture, operational health, resilience metrics, and strategic priorities. - Partner with Technology, Product, Security, Compliance, Internal Audit, Enterprise Risk Management, and Regulatory Affairs to ensure alignment with enterprise and regulatory requirements. - Oversee technology control governance activities, including standards compliance, audit readiness, risk assessments, control validation, and evidence management. - Drive the evolution of risk intelligence capabilities by leveraging operational data, analytics, automation, and insights to support proactive risk management and decision-making. - Champion operational resilience initiatives and ensure technology risks are considered throughout the lifecycle of products, services, platforms, and major technology change programs. - Lead organizational efforts to identify systemic control gaps, recurring operational issues, and opportunities to strengthen risk management effectiveness. - Establish and monitor meaningful risk, resilience, and governance metrics that provide leadership with actionable insights into technology performance and exposure. - Drive automation, process improvement, and modernization initiatives that reduce operational toil and improve efficiency across risk and governance processes. - Build, develop, and lead high-performing teams while fostering a culture of accountability, continuous learning, collaboration, and operational excellence. - Serve as a trusted advisor to executive leadership on technology risk strategy, resilience, governance, and operational readiness matters. This position is responsible for Cybersecurity and Information Security Risk Oversight of the Key Technology Services line of business, as well as technology and information security risk oversight for areas of the enterprise that manage technology, data and AI/ML systems. As part of this oversight role, experience with cybersecurity domains – including security operations, network and cloud security architecture, identity and access management, and cyber defenses – along with emerging AI security risk and AI governance frameworks.
